questions.q: What does "managed" mean in a Managed Disk?
options: Microsoft handles the underlying storage account; you only choose size and performance tier
The disk is managed entirely by the VM's own operating system
It refers to disks that can only be created through the Azure Portal, never the CLI
It means the disk is automatically deleted after 30 days
questions.explain: With Managed Disks, Microsoft handles storage-account placement and scaling behind the scenes, removing the old shared-storage-account IOPS ceiling problem.

questions.q: How many OS disks and data disks can a single Azure VM have?
options: Exactly one OS disk, and zero or more data disks
Multiple OS disks and exactly one data disk
Zero OS disks and one required data disk
Exactly one OS disk and exactly one data disk, no more
questions.explain: Every VM has exactly one OS disk holding the operating system, and can optionally attach one or more data disks for application data.

questions.q: Which disk tier is the cheapest, with higher and less consistent latency, best suited to backups or infrequently accessed data?
options: Ultra Disk
Premium SSD
Standard HDD
Standard SSD
questions.explain: Standard HDD is spinning-disk-backed and the most economical tier, fitting workloads that don't need fast, consistent storage.

questions.q: What distinguishes Ultra Disk from the other three performance tiers?
options: It is the cheapest tier available
It lets you adjust IOPS and throughput independently on the fly, without detaching the disk
It can only be used for OS disks, never data disks
It does not require a resource group
questions.explain: Ultra Disk is the top performance tier, allowing IOPS and throughput to be tuned independently and dynamically for the most demanding workloads.

questions.q: What VM size requirement applies to using Premium SSD or Ultra Disk?
options: No requirement — any VM size supports them
The VM must be in a Standard HDD-only region
The VM size must support premium storage, typically indicated by an "s" in the size name (e.g. Standard_D2s_v5)
The VM must be part of a Virtual Machine Scale Set
questions.explain: Premium and Ultra tiers require a VM size that supports premium storage — sizes with an "s" in the name, like Standard_D2s_v5.
